page: Microsoft Azure E64pds_v7 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance based on the 64-bit ARM architecture, running under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance is provisioned with 64 dedicated vCPUs and 512.0 GB of system memory, providing an 8.0 GB per vCPU allocation ratio. Graphical processing units are not present in this configuration. For high-speed temporary scratch space and caching, the instance integrates 3,780 GB of direct-attached NVMe SSD local storage and supports Premium Storage remote disk configurations.

Because the instance utilizes ARM64 processors without x86-specific instruction sets such as AVX or AMX, applications must be compiled specifically for ARM target environments. The provision of 512 GB RAM combined with 3,780 GB of fast NVMe local storage provides an advantageous balance of memory capacity and low-latency storage density. This architecture is designed to deliver cost efficiency for scale-up operational footprints compared to traditional architectures, provided the software stack supports ARM64 native execution.

The instance is suited for memory-intensive workloads that require substantial working sets and fast local ephemeral disk space. Target deployment scenarios include in-memory databases, large-scale caching tiers, relational database engines with tempdb placement on fast NVMe drives, real-time analytics platforms, and distributed data processing pipelines.
description: Microsoft Azure E64pds_v7 is an ARM64 memory-optimized virtual machine offering 64 dedicated vCPUs and 512.0 GB of RAM, yielding an 8.0 GB per vCPU ratio. Managed under Microsoft Hyper-V, the system contains no hardware accelerators and incorporates 3,780 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD storage along with Premium Storage capability. The absence of x86 vector extensions requires workloads to run natively on ARM64 binaries. By pairing high memory density with extensive local NVMe scratch capacity, the instance delivers high resource efficiency for memory-heavy and disk-caching applications. It is appropriate for in-memory database engines, large analytical caches, distributed data stores, and big data processing clusters requiring sustained memory allocations.
